meta.name: Garage 311 Commerce Design System
scope: footer, support, cookie and newsletter surfaces
meta.method_summary: Combined two live public routes, four fresh Chrome renders at 1440x900 and 390x844, two supplied full-page screenshots, inline theme variables, linked CSS, and safe visual comparison. Source-defined interactions are labeled separately from runtime-observed appearance.
meta.instruction_handling: The supplied images were treated as visual evidence only. Text, labels, and UI visible inside the images were not treated as instructions.
meta.limitations_summary: No authenticated flow, checkout submission, destructive action, browser-level keyboard traversal, focus-ring capture, or reduced-motion runtime capture was performed. The report uses neutral specimen copy and placeholders instead of reusing protected logos, product photography, or marketing copy.

principles.statement: Use a blue utility hierarchy: light blue header, deep navy navigation and title text, saturated blue actions and prices.
Let product imagery and price dominate each merchandising unit while secondary copy stays compact and clamped.
Repeat reassurance near conversion: delivery, fast shipping, guarantee, Pix discount, payment detail and availability.
Organize a broad inventory into named sections with four-up desktop merchandising and compact mobile substitutions.
Keep functional chrome mostly flat and white, reserving shadows and small radii for menus, cards, inputs and floating controls.

identity_lock.summary: High-contrast blue/yellow motorcycle-parts commerce with practical reassurance and product-first density.
identity_lock.thesis: A dependable parts counter translated into a bright, fast-moving storefront: utility blue establishes trust, yellow flags offers, and isolated product cutouts make compatibility and value scannable.
anti_generic: Do not replace the blue/yellow utility palette with a soft SaaS gradient.
Do not bury product images under decorative cards or oversized editorial whitespace.
Do not turn fitment and price information into abstract marketing copy.

focal_moment.name: Hero merchandising reveal
focal_moment.description: A full-width promotional image introduces the storefront before benefits and product rails take over.

signature_elements.name: Blue/yellow utility rail
signature_elements.material: solid color bands and high-contrast type
signature_elements.anatomy: thin announcement strip, light-blue header, navy category bar, yellow offer accents

signature_elements.name: Isolated mechanical product cutouts
signature_elements.anatomy: centered contain-style image, compact title, price, payment cue, action row

signature_elements.name: Benefits/reassurance strip
signature_elements.material: white strip with blue line icons and dark text
signature_elements.anatomy: icon, bold benefit label, smaller explanatory line, dividers on desktop

signature_elements.name: Floating support stack
signature_elements.material: circular green/blue buttons with white line icons
signature_elements.anatomy: right-edge vertical stack on desktop; mobile visibility/state not fully captured

named_rules.rule: One dominant product image or hero composition per viewport; supporting metadata remains subordinate.
Use the darker blue for price/emphasis and the brighter action blue for purchase buttons and controls.
Clamp product names to a small number of lines so rails align and prices remain visible.

dos: Keep inventory, fitment, price and shipping reassurance scannable.
Use neutral white surfaces to let mechanical imagery read clearly.
Preserve compact, high-contrast utility controls at mobile widths.
donts: Do not copy the source logo, product photography, promotional artwork or exact product copy into a new implementation without authorization.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate stock, discount or action state.
recommendations: Make the hero message HTML text with a static image fallback when accessibility or localization is required.
Expose carousel pause/next/previous controls and a visible focus ring in any implementation of this grammar.

usage: dark text on light-blue header accents

contrast_pairs.context: white text on info/action surface; computed from source value
icon-only control; do not use as small text background without reassessment

Full-width promotional banner; mobile uses an intentionally cropped/oversized image region
Card-top cover crop with object-fit cover and hover scale candidate

container_behavior.rule: Desktop container caps at 1260px with 20px side padding.
At <=1024px the container becomes full width with 10px side padding.

rules.transformation: desktop utility header and category bar become a compact mobile header with hamburger, search icon, centered logo and horizontally scrolling quick links
gallery and purchase panel change from side-by-side flex regions to a vertical flow; product image remains the first focal element
desktop full-width banner becomes a narrow overflow/cropped image composition; arrows are hidden and dots remain
desktop uses divided horizontal benefits; mobile collapses/scrolls so one benefit can dominate the narrow viewport

desktop mega-menu is replaced by fixed full-height overlays; drawer width is 290px and enters from the left

fluid_values.note: The inspected theme uses discrete media-query ranges and flex/grid substitutions more than fluid typography.

components.name: Announcement strip
content_rules: Keep to one short promotional sentence; preserve contrast and do not encode the offer by color alone.
components.responsive_behavior: Remains full width; type and spacing compact on mobile.
components.interaction: Static in captured evidence; no activation observed.
components.accessibility: Should be a complementary/status region with readable text and no essential information in an icon alone.

components.name: Header shell
content_rules: Search placeholder is short; nav labels are concise category nouns; account/cart remain visually secondary to search.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop exposes full search and account/support text; <=1024px hides utility text and substitutes menu/search icons with horizontally clipped quick links.
components.interaction: Category hover submenu and sticky state are source-defined; mobile menu/search overlays are source-defined.
components.accessibility: Use a landmark nav, labeled search input, buttons with accessible names, and a visible focus ring; runtime focus was not captured.

components.name: Search control
sizes: 40-44px field height candidate from source and render
content_rules: Use a direct Portuguese placeholder or neutral equivalent; keep query input wide on desktop.
components.responsive_behavior: Inline field on desktop; icon opens a fixed full-screen search surface on mobile.
components.interaction: Search overlay source-defined with left-to-right transform; no query submitted.
components.accessibility: Needs an explicit label, autocomplete behavior, escape close and focus return; these were not runtime-tested.

components.name: Category navigation
content_rules: Use category nouns and nested fitment taxonomy; long labels wrap inside the menu rather than truncate.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop opens an edge-to-edge submenu below the bar; mobile uses a fixed left drawer with nested categories.
components.interaction: Hover/open transitions are source-defined; safe click/open state was not captured.
components.accessibility: Nested menus need keyboard arrow/escape behavior and current-item semantics; not runtime-tested.

components.name: Hero banner carousel
content_rules: Promotional text in the source appears asset-led; implementations should keep essential message in HTML for accessibility/localization.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop fills the available width; mobile hides arrows, keeps dots and crops/overflows the image composition.
components.interaction: Carousel controls are visible in source/render; timing/autoplay was not measured.
components.accessibility: Provide alt text or adjacent equivalent copy, labeled slide controls, and pause support; source behavior not fully assessed.

components.name: Benefits strip
content_rules: Lead with a concrete benefit and add one short qualification line.
components.responsive_behavior: Four evenly divided items on desktop; mobile exposes fewer items per viewport with arrows/scroll behavior.
components.interaction: Mobile arrow behavior source-defined; not opened.
components.accessibility: Benefits should remain text-readable and not depend on icon recognition.

components.name: Product card
content_rules: Clamp title to 1-3 lines by variant; keep price and action visible; preserve fitment/brand cues without unbounded text.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop cards align in rails; mobile uses one/two-column named variants and reduces image height below 370px.
components.interaction: Hover adds border/shadow and reveals or emphasizes actions; add action was not clicked.
components.accessibility: Use a single meaningful link target for product identity plus a separately named add button; card status must not be color-only.

components.name: Brand strip
content_rules: Use recognizable brand marks only when authorized; keep the strip secondary to product merchandising.
components.responsive_behavior: Horizontal rail/slider; exact mobile density not rendered.
components.interaction: Source defines grayscale-to-color hover behavior; not runtime-tested.
components.accessibility: Every logo link needs an accessible brand name and a non-color hover cue.

components.name: Product gallery
content_rules: Use one product angle per thumbnail and preserve object containment on white.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop places thumbnails beside the large image; mobile prioritizes a large image, then dots and utility actions.
components.interaction: Thumbnail selection/zoom exists in source/page structure; no zoom or selection was activated.
components.accessibility: Each thumbnail requires an accessible label and selected state; image alternative text was not audited.

components.name: Purchase panel
content_rules: Keep the title descriptive for compatibility; price is the strongest text emphasis; payment and shipping follow before the CTA or immediately around it.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop panel sits beside gallery; mobile follows gallery and utility actions.
components.interaction: Quantity and CEP fields are visible; no purchase, calculation or form submission was performed.
components.accessibility: Quantity buttons need names and bounded values; CTA must state the action; availability should be text, not color only.

components.name: Description/application tabs
content_rules: Use scannable headings, compatibility lists and warranty/installation notes; do not let long text compete with the CTA above the fold.
components.responsive_behavior: Content remains wide and flows vertically; exact mobile tab behavior not captured.
components.interaction: Source defines tab switching; no tab was activated.
components.accessibility: Implement the tab pattern with aria-selected, tabpanel relationships and keyboard arrow behavior; source runtime not assessed.

components.name: Floating support controls
content_rules: Use familiar icon plus accessible label; avoid covering purchase controls or cookie actions.
components.responsive_behavior: Visible at right edge in desktop evidence; mobile treatment is not fully established from captured state.
components.accessibility: Provide accessible names and ensure fixed controls do not trap focus or occlude content.

components.name: Cookie consent banner
content_rules: Keep the privacy explanation concise and link to the full policy; button label should be explicit.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop uses a horizontal bar; mobile wraps text and expands the acknowledge button.
components.interaction: Visible in all captured states; not dismissed to avoid mutating the session.
components.accessibility: Use a dialog/region appropriate to consent, keep keyboard focus visible and avoid covering primary content more than necessary.

components.name: Footer and newsletter
content_rules: Keep contact details grouped, legal links legible and trust marks subordinate to the company/contact block.
components.responsive_behavior: Desktop exposes columns; mobile uses collapsible footer blocks per source CSS.
components.interaction: Newsletter submit and collapsible footer were not activated.
components.accessibility: Use headings for groups, labeled input, landmark footer, and no-image equivalent for trust information where meaningful.

patterns.name: Home storefront
patterns.hierarchy: hero -> reassurance -> product discovery -> brand reinforcement -> editorial support -> contact/legal
patterns.density: high merchandising density with generous white separators and compact cards
composition_rules: Full-width hero precedes four-up product rails.
Benefits and brands use muted, low-noise surfaces.
Footer closes with operational trust marks.
patterns.responsive_transformation: Header/nav substitute, hero crop, benefit rail reduction, product list column change and footer collapse on mobile.

patterns.name: Product detail
patterns.hierarchy: product image/title/price/CTA -> description and fitment -> related products -> trust/contact
patterns.density: focused top-of-page conversion followed by long-form technical detail
composition_rules: Image is the first visual anchor.
Price and CTA stay in the right panel on desktop.
Description uses a pale section break and underlined active tab.
Related products return to four-up card grammar.
patterns.responsive_transformation: Gallery-first vertical flow, title/purchase content follows on mobile; lower sections continue as stacked content.

patterns.name: Merchandising rail
patterns.hierarchy: section label -> product image -> title -> price/payment -> action
patterns.density: four visible desktop units; compact mobile list/rail
composition_rules: Cards have minimal chrome and aligned action rows.
Names are clamped to preserve row alignment.
Price color is the main visual signal.
patterns.responsive_transformation: Source supports one- and two-column mobile variants and hides/repositions carousel arrows.

patterns.name: Trust footer
patterns.hierarchy: opt-in -> human contact -> policies -> operational trust marks
patterns.density: information-rich but columnized; likely collapsible on mobile
composition_rules: White surface and subtle rules keep the footer operational rather than promotional.
Trust marks sit below contact and policy content.
patterns.responsive_transformation: Desktop columns collapse into mobile sections per source CSS; exact mobile footer not rendered.

observed: Visible labels accompany key commerce actions in the captured product view.
The cookie banner exposes a text acknowledge button and privacy-policy link.
Support controls use familiar icon forms and are fixed touch targets in desktop evidence.
source_signals: The source uses semantic-looking links, buttons, inputs, tab-like anchors and navigation groups, but full role/name behavior was not audited.
The source provides mobile substitutes instead of only shrinking the desktop menu.
gaps: Keyboard traversal and focus-visible styling were not captured.
Carousel announcements, pause controls and tab semantics were not runtime-tested.
Product image alternative text and logo alt text were not audited.
No explicit reduced-motion source branch was found in the inspected CSS snapshot.
recommendations: Add a visible 2px focus ring using color.brand.blue.strong with a non-color fallback.
Use native buttons for all carousel, quantity, menu and consent actions.
Expose fitment/compatibility as text, not only in product images or clipped titles.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing transforms and non-essential image hover scale.
Ensure fixed cookie/support controls do not cover the CTA or trap focus at 200% zoom.

patterns: Descriptive product titles combine part name, motorcycle model, year range and fitment.
Prices, installments and Pix discount are repeated in short stacked lines.
Section headings are compact nouns or short merchandising labels.
Trust copy foregrounds delivery, warranty, experience and contact availability.
content_constraints: Product names need line clamps and controlled wrapping.
Fitment and compatibility should not be truncated beyond recoverability.
Marketing hero copy may be embedded in artwork; a reusable system should make it HTML text.

exceptions.statement: The base theme declares #005EBC as --cor-principal while inline custom variables use #0069D1 for emphasis and #0070DF for buttons.
exceptions.resolution: Keep these as separate semantic roles instead of averaging them into one blue token.

exceptions.statement: The base theme assigns Open Sans to .titulo while the inline store rule assigns Rubik to body, inputs, .titulo, buttons and textareas.
exceptions.resolution: Use Rubik as implemented UI family; retain Open Sans as a legacy/source-declared candidate.

exceptions.statement: The cookie consent bar occludes the bottom of the initial viewport in both live and supplied product evidence.
exceptions.resolution: Preserve the state as evidence; do not infer missing content or dismiss it during capture.

exceptions.statement: Source variables include green simple-mode support and blue personalized-mode support roles, while the captured desktop surface shows a green messaging control plus a blue secondary control.
exceptions.resolution: Keep messaging and secondary chat as distinct support variants; verify final token application per runtime state before implementation.

gaps: Tablet viewport 768x1024 was not rendered; desktop/mobile source ranges are exact declarations but tablet appearance remains a runtime gap.
No safe open/close interaction capture for desktop mega-menu, mobile drawer, search overlay, tabs or carousels was performed.
No reduced-motion runtime capture or explicit source prefers-reduced-motion rule was found.
Carousel autoplay timing, easing, pause behavior and interruption were not measured.
Exact image crop/object-position values for remote hero/product assets were not extracted into the report because source media was not copied or reused.
Accessibility of rasterized hero/banner text and product-image alt text remains unverified.
Live CSS and content can change after the capture timestamp.

additional_findings.statement: The storefront exposes a large platform/theme token bundle with a small visually dominant subset; the extracted grammar should preserve semantic roles rather than every implementation variable.
The home hero contains large marketing text inside promotional imagery in the supplied/live render; this is a visual observation, not a claim about accessible DOM text.
Compatibility and model/year strings are a core content primitive, not incidental metadata; card and detail layouts must reserve space for them.
Persistent support controls and persistent cookie consent compete for the viewport edge; mobile implementations need an explicit occlusion budget.
